meta.title: Harold Kamgang — Process engineer, future QSE officer
meta.desc: Process engineering graduate. 19 months without a workplace accident on a 70-person site, 8% waste reduction, HACCP audit passed with no major finding. Looking for a work-study QSE placement, Grand Est, autumn 2026.
hero.role: Process engineering graduate — future QSE officer
hero.pitch: I ran safety for a 70-person production site on three shifts for 19 months without a single workplace accident. I'm looking for the apprenticeship that will let me do the same across a whole company.
hero.avail: 12-month apprenticeship · starts 20 October 2026 · 1 week school / 3 weeks company · mobile across Grand Est
stat.1.l: with no workplace accident, across 70 people on three shifts
about.p1: Trained as a process engineer, I spent two years in continuous production at an industrial flour mill in Cameroon, supervising 70 people across three shifts. That is where I learned that quality and safety are not decreed from an office: they are built on the floor, station by station, with the operators.
about.p2: I then added a dual degree to that operational base — an MSc in International Business at EAE Business School Barcelona and an MBA at Universitat de Lleida — to learn to speak the language of management as fluently as that of the shop floor. I am now preparing a Specialised Master's in QSE/CSR Strategy Management at CESI, and looking for the apprenticeship that will let me bring the two together.
tl.1.x: Master's thesis: a partner-led growth strategy for an electric bike tour operator.
tl.2.x: Safety for 70 people on three shifts, ISO 9001:2015 compliance, HACCP audit, continuous improvement and KPI-driven management.
tl.3.x: Wrote 10 standard operating procedures and their training materials, trained 70 operators, applied 5S.
tl.4.x: Restored inventory accuracy in a high-volume warehouse by reconciling physical stock against ERP records.
tl.5.x: Engineering thesis: a 0.92 correlation between sludge volume and lubricant consumption, a Pareto analysis identifying the six items of equipment behind 76 % of leaks, and a proposed UV detection system.
proj.lead: Seven concrete situations, described as context, action and result. Every figure is verifiable and I can walk through any of them in an interview.
proj.1.c: A continuous production site, 70 people across three shifts, in a milling environment where mechanical hazards and airborne dust are constant.
proj.1.a: Systematic team briefings, weekly floor visits, reporting and follow-up of near misses, PPE compliance checks, and involving every shift leader in the process rather than policing it from above.
proj.1.r: 19 consecutive months with no reported workplace accident — the entire time I was on site.
proj.2.t: HACCP audit passed with no major finding
proj.2.c: The site had to pass its food safety audit within a three-month window.
proj.2.a: A mock audit first, then identification of critical control points, traceability upgrades, resolution of the non-conformities found, and follow-through on the action plan until closure.
proj.2.r: Audit passed with no major finding, within the three-month deadline.
proj.3.t: 8% less waste and 10% more efficiency in 6 months
proj.3.c: High material losses on the line, with multiple and poorly documented causes.
proj.3.a: Supervised interns on root-cause analysis — Ishikawa diagrams and 5 Whys — standardised machine settings, applied 5S and tracked progress through indicators.
proj.3.r: 8% less waste and 10% more efficiency over six months, meaning several hundred tonnes of raw material saved.
proj.4.c: Rolling out the ISO 9001:2015 compliance programme across a site with several departments, each with its own habits.
proj.4.a: Risk assessment scored on severity and frequency, alignment of more than 30 stakeholders, drafting and updating of procedures.
proj.4.r: 100% audit readiness, and a quality approach the teams understood rather than endured.
proj.5.c: Weekly and monthly reporting produced by hand: slow, and a source of copying errors.
proj.5.a: Automation through Excel macros and Sage X3 ERP queries, then dashboards built for the management team.
proj.5.r: 40% less time spent on reporting, and decisions made on current data rather than last week's.
proj.6.c: Final Master's thesis, as a team of three, for an electric bike tour operator in Barcelona dependent on online travel agencies and their commissions.
proj.6.a: A multi-criteria partner selection framework, six field interviews and nine market sources, and standardisation of the commercial documentation set.
proj.6.r: A prioritised list of 20 partners, three incentive models and a 90-day pilot with measurable thresholds. Projected €38,500–€75,700 in incremental net revenue, aligned with SDGs 8, 11 and 17.
proj.7.c: A 216 MW gas power plant where oil leaks drove most of the maintenance workload, without anyone having quantified it.
proj.7.a: Correlated three years of production and maintenance data, ran a Pareto analysis on leak sources and an Ishikawa on the treatment unit failures.
proj.7.r: A 0.92 correlation established, six pieces of equipment identified as causing 76 % of leaks, and a UV detection system proposed. In 2021, 200 of 250 engine-room maintenance jobs were caused by oil leaks.

sk.1.d: PPE and safety management across three shifts

soft.lead: A list of adjectives proves nothing. Each quality below is tied to a real situation.
soft.1.p: Training 70 operators on 10 procedures does not happen through a memo. I learned to explain a technical requirement to someone who does not share my vocabulary — and to check it was understood before considering it applied.
soft.2.p: Six years of Toastmasters, including a term as VP Public Relations. That is what lets me run a safety briefing for a night shift, carry an initiative in front of 30-plus stakeholders, and present results to management without drowning them.
soft.3.p: An audit is prepared in three months, or it fails. Risk scoring, action plan, dates, owners: I have got into the habit of working with dated deliverables rather than intentions.
soft.4.p: When material losses rise, intuition is not enough. Ishikawa, 5 Whys, data pulled from the ERP: I trace the cause before proposing an action, and I measure afterwards.
soft.5.p: I have worked in Cameroon, studied in Spain, and I am moving to France. French and English are both native; German and Spanish are works in progress. I adapt to the person in front of me rather than the other way round.
edu.1.x: Admission is conditional on signing an apprenticeship contract — that is how the programme works.
edu.2.t: Dual degree — MSc International Business and MBA
edu.2.x: Two degrees from a single programme. Thesis: a partner-led growth strategy for Pink Ducks.
eng.1.p: A member for six years, including a term as vice-president for public relations. That is where I worked on public speaking, listening, and giving constructive feedback.
eng.2.p: Organising activities and leading youth groups — volunteer coordination, logistics and facilitation.
int.2: Soft mobility and cycling — the subject of my thesis

proj.8.t: Five years, five field projects — Saint-Jérôme Polytechnique
proj.8.c: A process engineering degree requiring a documented field project every year, from first to fifth.
proj.8.a: Dibamba thermal power plant, natural pesticide from nkui spices, composting coffee-roasting waste, wood-waste pyrolysis, Kribi oily water.
proj.8.r: Four projects out of five turned out to address the same question without my planning it: turn industrial waste into a resource, or stop it being produced. Degree awarded 15/20, with Distinction.
proj.9.c: A bike guide can only accompany one group at a time, in one language, and only during the tour. Personal project delivered to the founder of Pink Ducks.
proj.9.a: Full design and build in 42 hours across 20 phases: React Native and Firebase, a geofencing engine written from scratch, a six-language AI voice assistant, turn-by-turn navigation.
proj.9.r: A working prototype tested on real iPhone and Android handsets, delivered with its technical documentation and handover guide. The app warns about restricted zones before the fine: prevention, quite literally.
tl.6.r: Supervised project — energy recovery from waste
tl.6.x: Slow pyrolysis of wood waste into biochar: kinetic constants, reactor design, and treatment of the harmful gases the process emits. Two-person team.
tl.7.x: Unrecovered waste quantified at 2,794 kg a year, a lab composting trial across six samples over thirteen days, and a costed process yielding 30,000 FCFA margin per tonne.
tl.8.r: Practical work — sesame oil and natural pesticide
tl.8.x: Sesame oil production, and assisting on a natural pesticide made from nkui spices, including African pepper.
tl.9.r: First internship — thermal power plant operations
tl.9.x: Shift-based operations: inspection rounds, shift handovers, daily production reports and safety checks. First formal safety induction.
